marks.gloss_en: תא שמע: התולש צמר מבכור תם ... אסור -- טעמא דתולש, הא נתלש שרי, וכל שכן עולה דלא משהי לה (the a fortiori rides here; header)
(candidate answer) wool torn out of an unblemished burnt offering is permitted

הוא הדין אפילו נתלש נמי אסור; והאי דקתני תולש -- להודיעך כחו דעקביא, דבבעל מום אפילו בתולש נמי שרי. Itself challenged and defended (26b.4, schema gap -- header): והאנן נשר תנן! -- תנא נשר להודיעך כחן דרבנן, תנא תולש להודיעך כחו דעקביא
how long must an Israelite tend the firstborn? a small animal -- thirty days
the firstborn is eaten year by year (within its year), whether unblemished or blemished

דאמר קרא 'בכור בניך תתן לי', 'כן תעשה לצאנך'; 'מלאתך ודמעך לא תאחר', 'כן תעשה לשורך' (26b.10-11) -- the firstborn-son clause is paired with the flock and the first-fruits clause with the ox. Per Steinsaltz (not stated in the Hebrew): as the son is redeemed at thirty days so the flock at thirty; as first-fruits come at Shavuot, fifty days on, so the ox at fifty

איפוך אנא! -- reverse the pairing (the ox at thirty, the flock at fifty). The exchange that follows rides here (header: gate gap): the stam answers מסתברא דמקדם למקדם, דמאחר לדמאחר (the earlier clause to the earlier animal, the later to the later), and counters itself אדרבה, דסמיך ליה לדסמיך ליה! (on the contrary, the adjacent clause to the adjacent animal) -- left unanswered; the sugya turns to אלא אמר רבא
ואימא: שיתין! -- [if the ox gets another 'doing'] say sixty [days]!
לא מסרך הכתוב אלא לחכמים -- Scripture handed [the measure] only to the sages
Rava: the verse says 'you shall DO' [so you shall do with your ox] (Shemot 22:29)
the priests, Levites and poor who assist at the shepherd's, the threshing floor and the slaughterhouse -- one does not give them teruma and tithe as their wage
and lest you say there is no death [for it] -- 'and you shall not die': the desecration carries death
the Sages wished to fine them, that teruma be separated on their account from [other, untithed] produce -- and they did not fine them
and in all of them the owner has the benefit of discretion (טובת הנאה)
תניא נמי הכי -- the baraita too reads 'תעשה' as another 'doing' with the ox, as Rava did
(entertained) 'the firstborn of your sons you shall give Me', 'so shall you do with your flock' -- might one think the same [period] for your ox too?
from here they said: how long must Israelites tend the firstborn? a small animal -- thirty days
if the priest said within the period 'give it to me', he shall not give it to him
the cited mishnah lemma on dangling wool of a firstborn (per Steinsaltz: what appears with the fleece is permitted, what does not appear with it is forbidden)
R' Ile'a: Reish Lakish holds [so] because it is impossible for a fleece to be without dangling strands
